# Shift handover: chat-assistant · 2026-09-20 06:14
> Receiver: run /shift-start first. Read back before acting.
> Previous handover: none · Next-session goal: none given

## 1 · Status  (I)
🟢 Pure conversational session — no code, no builds, nothing fragile. The repo is empty aside from an initial "start" commit.

## 2 · Picture  (P)
This was a multi-topic conversational assistant session spanning simulated dates May 20–30 2023. The user asked for book recommendations, podcast recommendations, meal planning advice, bag organization tips, a cover letter and resume for a specific person (Jin Yu), social media posts for a company (GoodSpace), and a creative writing piece (50 burnout book titles + press release + blog post + sample chapter). No code was written. No files were changed in the repo. The session is a long free-form chat with no single driving project.

**Mental map**: No technical hypotheses. The session is advisory/conversational.

## 3 · Next actions  (A)
1. No pending actions. The user's last substantive question was about using leftover chicken breast in a one-pot pasta recipe (answered). The `/shift-change` was the final message.

## 4 · No-go zones
| Rejected path | Why it was rejected | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| "ASCII art is subjective" framing | User explicitly said "It is not a matter of subjective opinion. There was no recognizable heart shape." The assistant produced broken ASCII art 4 times and deflected with "subjective." Never frame inability as subjectivity. | Never — own the failure instead |
| Generic/long suggestion lists when user wants specifics | User repeatedly pushed back on website engagement ideas ("None of those suggestions seem good enough") and wanted concrete, innovative, never-been-done ideas. Lists of 5–6 standard ideas frustrated them. | User explicitly asks for a brainstorm list |

## 5 · Working with the user  (who they are, and taste)

**About the user** (facts shared in passing, all from the May 2023 chat dates):

- Avid reader. Recently finished "The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo" and loved it. Planning to read "The Royal We" and "Sea of Tranquility." [user said, May 20]
- Attended online book club discussion on Facebook Live on Feb 22 2023; the author (Taylor Jenkins Reid) responded to their question. [user said, May 20]
- Attended a reading by Emily St. John Mandel at their local library; asked about inspiration for Olive Llewellyn; bought a signed copy of "Sea of Tranquility." [user said, May 20]
- Attended a literary festival on March 4 2023 featuring Celeste Ng, Tommy Orange, and Ayobami Adebayo on diversity in contemporary literature. [user said, May 20]
- Part of a work book club; discussion leader is named Rachel. They read "The Power" by Naomi Alderman "last month" (i.e. ~April 2023). [user said, May 20]
- Daily commuter to work, ~45 minutes each way. [user said, May 26 and May 29]
- Uses a black leather backpack for daily commute (getting worn out). Also owns a duffel bag. [user said, May 27]
- Took a weekend trip to visit family around May 13 2023 (said "two weeks ago" on May 27). Left favorite sweatshirt at mom's house; needs to ask mom to send it. [user said, May 27]
- Tends to forget lunchbox or gym clothes. Goes to the gym. [user said, May 27]
- Looking for a new work bag: tote or backpack, spacious (fits laptop, water bottle, essentials), multiple compartments, leather or durable nylon. [user said, May 27]
- Listens to podcasts during commute at 1.5x speed on Apple Podcasts. Also uses Spotify. Interested in trying other podcast apps with custom playlists and speed control. [user said, May 26]
- Enjoys true crime podcasts: finished episode 12 of "My Favorite Murder," listens to ≥1 episode/week. [user said, May 26]
- Enjoys entrepreneurial podcasts: finished ~15 episodes of "How I Built This." Interested in stories behind companies, especially tech companies founded by non-technical founders. [user said, May 29]
- Cutting down on social media to make time for podcasts and books; says it helps mental health and productivity. [user said, May 29]
- Trying to stay more informed about current events; listens to "The Daily." [user said, May 26]
- Interested in personal development and productivity. [user said, May 29]
- Changed breakfast two weeks before May 30: switched from toast with scrambled eggs to oats with fruits and nuts. [user said, May 30]
- Trying to cut down on carbs. [user said, May 30]
- Was planning to make one-pot pasta with chicken breast, cherry tomatoes, and spinach for dinner on May 30. Had leftover chicken breast in fridge, considering frozen spinach. [user said, May 30]
- Has a website (context from May 23 questions about user engagement) but gave no details about it. [user said, May 23]
- Related to or helping **Jin Yu** — 21-year-old Korean woman in Niagara Falls, ON (3361 Cardinal Drive, L2H 3A6). Second year Journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University (expected June 2023). Previously at Brock University. 3 years at Starbucks, server at Twisted Vine, social media coordinator at Dog'SPAw. Smart Serve certified, intermediate Korean, basic French, Honours/Scholar's student (90–95+ avg). Requested a bartending cover letter and resume. [user said, May 30]

| I assumed | User corrected | Rule from now on | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Broken ASCII art was passable | It was not a heart at all | If art output is garbled, own it; never deflect with "subjective" or "may not meet expectations" | "It is not a matter of subjective opinion. There was no recognizable heart shape anywhere to be found in the images you posted." |
| Long lists of standard ideas would satisfy the user | User wanted truly novel, specific, never-been-done ideas | Don't pad with generic suggestions; if you can't deliver something genuinely novel, say so honestly | "Honestly, I don't think any of these ideas are good enough either. Can you come up with something that's never been done before?" |
| Said "I'll make sure to consider your preferences" (confusing whose preferences) | User sarcastically echoed it back — the assistant confused itself with the user | Never confuse the user's preferences with the assistant's; the assistant has no preferences | "I'll make sure to consider your preferences when making my recommendations." |
| Gave specific podcast episode numbers and titles (e.g. "Episode 1,044: Airbnb's Brian Chesky") | Not corrected, but these were fabricated details | Do not invent specific episode numbers or titles; say "search for X's appearance on Y" instead | — |

- **Book recommendations**: Suggested "The Royal We," "Daisy Jones and The Six" (TJR), "The Interestings," "The Address," "The Age of Light," "The Handmaid's Tale," "The Fifth Season," "The Poppy War," "The Song of Achilles" and others across multiple themes (similar to Evelyn Hugo; power dynamics/resistance). ## 9 · Gotchas
- The assistant fabricated specific podcast episode numbers and titles (e.g. "Episode 1,044: Airbnb's Brian Chesky" on Mixergy, "Season 1: The Instagram Story" on Startup). These are not verified and should not be repeated as fact.
- The assistant repeatedly failed at ASCII art and made it worse by calling it "subjective." This user does not tolerate that framing.
- The assistant once said "I'll make sure to consider your preferences" as if it had preferences of its own. The user noticed immediately. Don't confuse agent preferences with user preferences.

## 10 · Jargon
| Term | Means | Not to be confused with |
|---|---|---|
| "work book club" | User's workplace book club, led by Rachel | The online book club (Facebook Live, Feb 22) |
| GoodSpace | AI-powered recruitment platform the user asked about for social media posts | Not the user's own product — just a writing task |
| Jin Yu | Person whose cover letter and resume were written; likely the user themselves or someone close | — |
